correctness.rationale: The Moore determinant factors as the product of all distinct Fq-rational hyperplane forms because each factor divides and their total degree equals that of the nonzero determinant. Near coordinate-span rank r the vanishing factors form an m=N−r dimensional Moore determinant times a unit. If Q=q^(m−1), all determinant monomials lie in (y_i^Q), giving upper ν bound by Frobenius powers; the unique lex-leading determinant monomial to power H−1, H=p^(s−a(m−1)), gives nonvanishing modulo (y_i^(p^s)), giving exact ν and fpt=1/Q. Rank-locus component and extension-field counts follow from kernel Gaussian choices and quotient injections; the q^s−1 scalar action is free. Independent checks at q=2 small sizes and source finite polynomial tests corroborate boundary m=1 and cone m=N.
